enospc.firstboot_plan: T1-T7 failed before package installation for their recorded source, allowlist, apt-plan, runner-permission, or bounded-query failures. T8 passed 15 source checks, obtained authenticated metadata for 18 packages, passed apt_guard, and its install command returned success before the host inventory keyring check failed. K1 later recorded the exact keyring and ancestor metadata. T9 used the independently reviewed V11 source: all source checks, authenticated APT metadata (18 records), the apt plan and guard, and the install command status checks passed. T9 then failed during host inventory with ambiguous package ownership for `/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2`. The staged keyring cleanup reported `removed` with matching identities and hash. Neither T8 nor T9 reached image download or QEMU boot. T10 then passed 18/18 payload hash entries within 20 published files, completed package setup and installation (18 packages), and failed closed during host inventory on the libaio alias query. Its resolved canonical path was recorded but not queried; owner remains UNKNOWN. Keyring cleanup succeeded. No image download or cgroup/QEMU/guest step occurred. V13's explicit canonical-path fallback is under development and unactivated. V13 parser source review is CLEAR (51 focused tests), but activation was held before T11 by independent kernel/source-compatibility analysis: the observed controller process occupies a populated non-root service cgroup, which cannot distribute the required domain memory controller. This is a source-level incompatibility; no cgroup failure or runtime EACCES was observed. V14 independently passed 55 focused source tests and received CLEAR review (source-only); runtime/topology remains unobserved. It uses the already-enabled root cgroup as a read-only control parent and records the service cgroup separately as source identity. Activation awaits a fresh all-22-file stage. Author staging is on hold pending the report and a new base. No T11 run has occurred.

This is a source-level incompatibility established from the recorded hierarchy and kernel rule; no runtime cgroup failure or EACCES was observed. V14 source review is independently CLEAR with 55 focused tests, source-only; runtime/topology remains unobserved and activation awaits a fresh all-22-file stage. V14 proposes the existing root cgroup as a read-only control parent, with the service cgroup recorded separately as source identity; no global ancestor changes, root QEMU, or moving other processes. Author staging is on hold pending the report and a new base. No T11 run has occurred. G0, E1 and E2 remain zero.
